My sister lets the power go to her head and while she can generally make my little brother obey her she has a tougher time with me. I protested as best as I could but she wasn't having it and grounded me for disobeying my sister who is a pseudo parent while they are away. I just dropped it cause its not worth arguing any point with my mom. AITA here? EDIT:My brother told me afterwards that he was the one that told mom, I forgave him cause I mean I can't be mad at that little turd for too long

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. My parents left for a class thing and a business trip, so we're alone at home: me, my sister, and my brother. My sister is 18, I'm 17, and my brother is 12. My parents left my sister in charge, which I guess is because she's the oldest. But I don't really think she's ready for that responsibility. She's been acting a bit bossy, especially with me. On Sunday, I wanted to go out with my girlfriend for dinner. My sister told me I couldn't leave. When I asked why, she said, "Because I said so." At first, I thought she was joking, so I laughed. But she wasn't, and she kept insisting. I told her she can boss around my little brother but not me, and I went out anyway. When I came home, my brother had called our mom and told her we were fighting. My mom called me and said I'm grounded and have to do what my sister says because she's in charge. I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't having it. I ended up dropping it because I didn't want to argue further. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by going out despite my sister's objections. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) here? First, I need to consider the roles here. My sister was left in charge by our parents, so technically, she's supposed to be the authority figure when they're away. But she's only 18, and I'm 17. I'm not sure if she's mature enough to handle that responsibility, especially with me. I went out with my girlfriend, which is something I wanted to do. My sister told me I couldn't, but I didn't take her seriously at first. When I realized she was serious, I still went out. That might have been a mistake because she was supposed to be in charge. However, I also think that being in charge doesn't mean she can control my actions entirely. I'm almost an adult, and I should have some freedom. But at the same time, I understand that when parents leave someone in charge, they expect that person to enforce rules and maintain order. The fact that my brother called our mom and told her we were fighting complicates things. It seems like my brother was scared or thought things were getting out of hand. My mom, upon hearing this, grounded me and made me follow my sister's orders. I tried to protest, but my mom wasn't listening. I ended up dropping it, which might have been the right move to avoid further conflict. But I'm still unsure if I did the right thing by going out in the first place. I also need to consider the consequences. By going out, I disobeyed my sister, who was in charge, and that led to me being grounded. My mom's reaction was to support my sister, which shows that she trusts her judgment. On the other hand, I feel like I was being reasonable by wanting to go out with my girlfriend. It's a normal activity for someone my age. But I also understand that when parents are away, they expect their children to follow the rules set by the person in charge. I'm also thinking about how this affects our relationship. My sister might feel more empowered now, knowing that my mom supports her. But I might feel resentful because I was grounded for something I thought was a minor issue. In the end, I'm torn between respecting the authority my parents gave to my sister and asserting my own independence. I want to be responsible and follow the rules, but I also want to have some freedom. I guess I need to communicate better with my sister and maybe talk to my parents about how they can support both of us in handling this responsibility. But for now, I'm just trying to figure out if I was in the wrong by going out with my girlfriend despite my sister's objections.
